Releases are cut by pushing a git tag named `vYYYY.MM.N`, for example `v2026.09.2`. The `N` is the release counter within that month.

```
git tag v2026.10.1
git push origin v2026.10.1
```

CI then builds and publishes. Don't publish by hand.

The only source for this is a shared project memory (convention, human-authored). The repo has no CI config (no `.github/`), no release docs and no release targets in the `Makefile`. I couldn't check what the CI pipeline does or which checks run before publishing. I also couldn't confirm whether `N` restarts at 1 each month, though the example format suggests it does.

Today is 2026-10-01, so if nothing has shipped yet this month, the next tag would be `v2026.10.1`. Check existing tags first with `git tag -l 'v2026.10.*'` to pick the right `N`.
